newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso on pioneer visit to South Africa.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso on pioneer visit to South Africa.

text.p: President Fernando Henrique Cardoso heads for South Africa on Sunday on the first visit to that country by a Brazilian leader.

Cardoso's three-day visit, following a one-day stop in Angola, is aimed at defrosting decades of icy relations that resulted from Brazil's vigorous opposition to South Africa's former policy of apartheid, diplomats said.

"The visit above all is aimed at raising the level of political dialogue," said Jose Vicente Pimentel, head of the Africa Department in the Brazilian Foreign Ministry. "We also place great importance on the fact that Cardoso will be accompanied by a delegation of more than 70 businessmen."
South African diplomats said Cardoso's tour, which will take him to Johannesburg, Pretoria and Cape Town, was significant because it is the first by a Brazilian president.

"We regard this as a great step forward in relations between our two countries," Andre Nel, an official at Pretoria's embassy in Brasilia, told Reuters. "It is extremely significant in that for so many years we have been isolated due to the previous policy of apartheid."

Cardoso will meet South African President Nelson Mandela on Nov. 26 and the two leaders are expected to sign several accords including an agreement to protect investments. Pimentel told reporters the accords would be the first ever to be signed by leaders of the two countries.
South African foreign direct investment in Brazil totals some $1.0 billion, with both sides hoping greater investor security will double that sum over the next four years.

After meeting Mandela, Cardoso will go to Johannesburg, where he will attend a business seminar and deliver a speech. On Nov. 28, he heads for Cape Town for talks with Archbishop Desmond Tutu, chairman of South Africa's post-apartheid Truth Commission.

Cardoso will spend a day in Angola before he goes to South Africa. In Angola, tied to Brazil through the Portuguese language, he will visit Brazilian troops taking part in a United Nations peacekeeping operation and hold talks with President Jose Eduardo dos Santos.
